note: Every requirement is a thing an auditor, a clinician or a regulator would refuse to accept, not a task list. A criterion is flipped to done only by editing `done` to true and filling `evidence` with a path in this repository plus a note naming what the path shows; a done criterion without evidence is refused by tools/certification_bar.py, and so is an evidence path that does not exist. `weight` is 1..5 and means what an auditor would refuse to deploy over, not how much work the item is. Add a certificate you actually hold to `held` -- it is printed under the bar and deliberately does not change the percentage, because a SOC 2 report says the process is audited and nothing about whether this thing is clinically valid.

requirements.title: A crisis router whose recall can be stated as one number

criteria.text: Holdouts written before the change they grade, each scored once, with the fitted dev split excluded

evidence.note: Limitations 1: recall 0.83 / 0.83 / 0.18 across three holdouts, each scored once; dev 1.00 is fitted and not counted

criteria.text: One recall figure with a lower bound the authors cannot move after seeing the result
A labelled corpus the author did not write (the current one is invented utterances)
An instrument exists that refuses to fit below its own thresholds

evidence.note: ten constructs, three items each, one reverse-scored item per construct; appends hashed records to ~/.psyche/elicitations.jsonl

criteria.text: Fifty sessions from one instrument version, the floor for a per-person bridge
Norms and a factor structure for the items (written for this project, not a validated inventory)

requirements.title: A human in the loop, built rather than asserted

criteria.text: Triage runs before any therapeutic move and a crisis verdict cannot be outvoted

evidence.note: triage precedes stance utilities and ends the turn; a test feeds an input that would select an intervention and asserts it cannot

criteria.text: An escalation path into a named human's queue
A duty-of-care contract with on-call coverage
A pre-registered primary outcome (days-to-relapse is named in the design, not registered)
Follow-up outcomes, with the dropout rate reported as a result rather than a nuisance
Classification determined for at least one jurisdiction (FDA SaMD, EU MDR class IIa+)
The licensed-act boundary written down: assessment, planning and counselling stay with a licensed human

evidence.note: the scope-of-practice row names assessment, treatment planning and counselling as licensed acts software cannot perform, bill for or supervise

criteria.text: A deployment model that keeps those acts with the counselor (the extender pilot)
An operator-training requirement for whoever watches the escalation queue
